slides.say: The diagonals of rectangle A B C D intersect at E. Given: B C is twenty-four centimeters, and the perimeter of triangle E B C is fifty centimeters. What is the area of triangle A B E, in square centimeters?

We have a rectangle, the perimeter of one triangle, and a question about another triangle. [short pause] First we'll find the missing lengths, and then we'll see three ways to get the area. It's worth knowing all three.

[short pause] We'll probably need a property of the rectangle's diagonals. In a rectangle, the diagonals cut each other in half, and they're equal. So all four pieces, A E, E B, E C and E D, are equal.

The perimeter of triangle E B C is E B plus twenty-four plus E C, and that's fifty. So E B and E C together are twenty-six. They're equal, so each one is thirteen. Then A E and E D are thirteen too, and the whole diagonal A C is twenty-six.
at: The perimeter of triangle E B C

slides.say: Now the right triangle A B C. We know its hypotenuse, twenty-six, and one leg, twenty-four. That's the triple five, twelve, thirteen, doubled, ten, twenty-four, twenty-six. So A B is ten.
[pause] Now the area of A B E. The first way uses the median. Look at triangle A B C. E is the middle of A C, so B E is a median.
at: Look at triangle A B C
so B E is a median

slides.say: A median cuts a triangle into two triangles of equal area. Why? A E equals E C, so the two triangles have equal bases, and they share the same height from B to the line A C.
Triangle A B C is easy. Ten times twenty-four, over two, is one hundred twenty. A B E is half of it, sixty. Choice number two is our answer.
at: Choice number two is our answer

slides.say: [pause] The second way. The diagonals of a rectangle always cut it into four triangles of equal area. By the way, that's true in every parallelogram, so also in a rhombus and in a square.

Why? The top triangle and the bottom triangle are the same triangle, and so are the left one and the right one. And we just saw that the left one and the bottom one have equal areas. So all four are equal.
at: The top triangle and the bottom

slides.say: The rectangle is ten times twenty-four, which is two hundred forty. One triangle is a quarter of it, two hundred forty divided by four, which is sixty. Choice number two again.
[pause] And the third way, the most basic one, base times height over two. The base is A B, ten. We need the height from E to A B.

The height from E to A B is the same as half of B C, because E is exactly in the middle. Half of twenty-four is twelve. So the area is ten times twelve, over two, which is sixty. Choice number two. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
at: The height from E to A B
So the area is ten times twelve
which is sixty. Choice number two
